description: FEHM is Los Alamos National Laboratory's subsurface heat and mass transfer code. It contains flow and transport formulations for fractured or unfractured porous media, including multiphase fluids, heat transfer and optional displacement calculations. Inputs describe a subsurface domain and its material, fluid and boundary conditions; outputs describe simulated thermal, flow and transport responses. Spatial coverage ranges from local reservoirs to groundwater domains, with mesh and time resolution chosen by the user. Free BSD-3-Clause Fortran source includes build instructions and verification suites. A limitation is compiler sensitivity in legacy code: the README reports incomplete runs in six verification cases with Intel Classic 2021.12.0. FEHM supports geothermal, geological storage, groundwater protection and waste-isolation simulations. Waiwera (model-waiwera) is a related geothermal simulator. The repository documents development and tests, but this review did not run them or verify a particular site's predictions.
